title: Ice Cream Sundae with Fruit Topping

content.title: About
content.content: Ice cream sundae with fruit topping is a classic dessert consisting of vanilla ice cream scoops drenched in rich chocolate sauce and generously topped with fresh fruits, berries, and sometimes nuts. The fruit topping adds sweetness, a hint of acidity, and a vibrant color palette.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first sundae appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a street‑side treat.
Traditional fruit toppings often include strawberry, banana, kiwi and blueberry.
In some countries the sundae is served with caramel sauce instead of chocolate.
Vegan versions use coconut‑milk ice cream and unsweetened fruit purees.

items.title: Vitamins and Antioxidants
items.content: Fresh fruits are rich in vitamin C, vitamin A and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: The dairy base of the ice cream supplies calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy Boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from the fruit and fats from the ice cream quickly replenish energy after physical activity.

items.title: Dietary Fiber
items.content: Fruits add dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Sugar Content
items.content: Both ice cream and fruit topping can be high in sugar, which is a concern for diabetics or those watching their weight.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: Traditional ice cream contains lactose; lactose‑intolerant individuals should choose dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Nut Allergy
items.content: If nuts are included in the topping, they may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.

items.title: Fruit Acidity
items.content: Acidic fruits can irritate sensitive teeth or the stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sundae in tall glasses, layering ice cream, sauce and fruit. Top with whipped cream, chopped nuts or sprinkles. For a lighter version, use frozen berries instead of fresh fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ice cream in the freezer at –18 °C in an airtight container. Store the fruit topping separately in the refrigerator and use within 2‑3 days.
